paper_metadata.title: A More General Quantum Credit Risk Analysis Framework

summary: The paper proposes an enhanced quantum credit risk analysis algorithm using iterative quantum amplitude estimation with a multi‑factor default model and arbitrary (non‑integer) LGD encoding. A noiseless simulation of a 2‑asset, 2‑factor portfolio used 9 qubits and ~50,000 IQAE samples, while noisy experiments on IBM devices (ibm_perth, ibm_lagos, ibm_canberra, ibm_algiers) used 7–13 qubits for portfolios with 2–4 assets but failed to produce reliable estimates due to decoherence.

experiments.description: Noiseless simulation of the enhanced quantum credit risk analysis algorithm using the multiple-rotations multi-factor uncertainty model on a two-asset, two-risk-factor toy portfolio, with iterative quantum amplitude estimation to estimate VaR at 95% confidence.

algorithm.variant: iterative quantum amplitude estimation (IQAE) for VaR estimation
algorithm.convergence_criteria: target precision ϵ = 0.002 and 99% target confidence interval

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Default states of two assets are encoded in qubits; two qubits are used to discretize each standard normal risk factor; controlled rotations encode default probabilities under the multi-factor model.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate VaR_α by finding the smallest x such that P[L ≤ x] ≥ α, where L = Σ_k PD_k·LGD_k under the multi-factor default model.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Bisection search over threshold x using the amplitude-estimation subroutine; no penalty formulation.

problem_instance.description: Toy credit portfolio with two assets and two systemic risk factors; LGD values are non-integer to demonstrate arbitrary-LGD support.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Noiseless classical simulation of the Qiskit circuit; no external dataset preprocessing reported.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Single noiseless simulation run reported; VaR estimated via IQAE and bisection search.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Bisection search over the estimated CDF to obtain VaR_α.

speedup_claims.conditions: for quantum amplitude estimation / iterative quantum amplitude estimation used to estimate VaR
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the quadratic speedup claim but does not provide a direct empirical runtime comparison for this noiseless simulation.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: IQAE query complexity bounded by 1.4/ϵ · ln( (2/γ) log2(π/(4ϵ)) )
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Monte Carlo methods for VaR estimation; paper does not give a specific asymptotic bound here
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: Approximately 50,000 quantum samples for the reported precision/confidence setting

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not estimated in the paper; experiment uses a toy instance with K=2 assets and 2 risk factors.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require large-scale fault‑tolerant hardware capable of executing tens of thousands of Grover/QAE iterations with deep circuits encoding large portfolios.
limiting_factors: Deep circuits required for amplitude-estimation-based risk evaluation
No empirical comparison with classical Monte Carlo runtime

notes: No circuit depth or gate counts were reported for the noiseless simulation.
Hardware is a classical simulator back-end in Qiskit, not a real QPU.
The paper states that QAE provides quadratic speedup over Monte Carlo but does not demonstrate empirical advantage.
Experiment is a small noiseless simulation used to illustrate the algorithm.

experiments.description: Noisy simulations and real-hardware executions of the enhanced multi-factor quantum credit risk algorithm across multiple portfolio sizes and IBM superconducting QPUs, used to study noise, topology, and scalability effects.

algorithm.variant: iterative quantum amplitude estimation (IQAE) with multi-factor uncertainty model and arbitrary-LGD encoding
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Not explicitly stated; experiments executed for multiple configurations to observe noise and hardware effects

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Multi-factor default model encoded with multiple rotations; arbitrary LGD handled via LinearAmplitudeFunction instead of a weighted sum register; configurations vary from 2 to 4 assets and 1 to 3 systemic risk factors.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate expected loss / VaR-related quantities for the credit portfolio under the enhanced quantum CRA framework.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Bisection search and amplitude-estimation subroutine; arbitrary-LGD support implemented by piecewise linear amplitude function rather than integer-weight sum register.

problem_instance.description: Family of toy credit-risk instances with realistic LGD values generated by domain experts; used to benchmark hardware behavior under increasing circuit size.

dataset_specification.description: Public repository with generated credit-risk benchmark data; configurations span 2-4 assets and 1-3 systemic risk factors.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Data generated by domain experts to reflect realistic input measurements; no further preprocessing details reported.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Experiments run on actual machines and on classical simulations of the machines’ noise models; aggregate results reported across configurations, with ratio of estimated expected loss to maximum possible loss plotted.

noise_model.noise_type: hardware noise / simulator noise models from IBM QPUs
noise_model.mitigation_details: Noise-model simulations were run for each hardware configuration to validate the noise models; no explicit mitigation method reported.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Expected loss estimated directly from the objective qubit; ratio to maximum possible loss used for analysis.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Results concentrated toward half of the maximum possible loss under noise/decoherence

results.value: converged toward half of the maximum possible loss

speedup_claims.conditions: IQAE-based VaR estimation under the enhanced multi-factor credit risk framework
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not report an empirical speedup on hardware; instead it reports noise/decoherence effects and scalability limitations.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: IQAE query complexity bounded by 1.4/ϵ · ln( (2/γ) log2(π/(4ϵ)) )
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Monte Carlo methods for VaR estimation; paper does not give a specific asymptotic bound here
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: Example given: around 28,000 applications of the Grover operator for 99.9% confidence and 0.05% target error

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not estimated; current experiments involve only 2–4 assets and 7–13 qubits.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require substantially longer qubit coherence times and far deeper executable circuits to run many IQAE iterations reliably.
limiting_factors: Results converge toward ~50% default probability due to noise
Quadratic speedup insufficient under realistic error-correction costs

notes: The paper reports qubit ranges (7 to 13) for the configurations but does not provide explicit circuit depth or gate counts.
The experiment includes both real QPU runs and noisy simulations; hardware.type is set to real_qpu_superconducting because actual IBM superconducting devices were used.
Section 4 reports that noise causes results to converge toward half of the maximum loss, preventing extraction of correct expected values.
Authors explicitly state that current circuit depth and coherence limitations hinder meaningful results.
